title: Sequential Cleanup Interruption (Clean-up Leak)
pattern: Multiple fallible resource release calls (e.g., `.close()`, `.flush()`) executed sequentially in a single cleanup block, where an exception thrown by an earlier release halts the execution of subsequent releases.
why_bad: Resource leak. An exception trying to close the statement (e.g., due to a socket error) aborts the cleanup block, preventing the underlying connection from being returned to the pool or closed. [34, p. 30]
detection: A `finally` or cleanup block containing sequential method calls known to throw checked exceptions, where prior calls are not isolated in their own try-catch scopes.
counterexample: Cleanups where resources are managed via automatic RAII (such as Rust's automatic dropping) or modern Java `try-with-resources`.
source: *Michael T. Nygard - Release It!*, Section 2.5, p. 30 [34]
